title: U.S. House · Texas's 16th District
area: El Paso and surrounding El Paso County, in far West Texas.

context.text: Incumbent Veronica Escobar (D) ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary. Adam Bauman won the Republican nomination in a May 26, 2026 primary runoff, defeating Manuel Barraza.

candidates.name: Veronica Escobar

summary.text: Veronica Escobar is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Texas's 16th District. A former El Paso County Commissioner and County Judge, she serves on the House Appropriations, Budget, Judiciary and Armed Services committees.

background.text: Born in El Paso, Texas, in 1969; earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas in 1991 and a master's degree in English Literature from New York University in 1993.
Worked as a professor, a nonprofit executive, and communications director for the mayor of El Paso's office before entering elected office.
Served as an El Paso County Commissioner from 2006 to 2010 and as El Paso County Judge from 2011 to 2017.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, the Committee on the Budget, the Committee on the Judiciary, and the Committee on Armed Services in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Adam Bauman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff over Manuel Barraza.

summary.text: Adam Bauman is the Republican nominee challenging Escobar. He is a U.S. Navy Special Warfare Combatant Crewman veteran who also served in the U.S. Border Patrol's BORTAC tactical team, campaigning on lower property taxes, border security, and veterans' issues.

background.text: Served as a U.S. Navy Special Warfare Combatant Crewman (Navy SWCC).
Served in the U.S. Border Patrol as part of the Border Patrol Tactical Team (BORTAC).

priorities.text: Lowering El Paso property taxes, which he says are among the highest in Texas.
Supporting Customs and Border Protection's mission to secure the border.
Expanding care and benefits for military veterans.

positions.summary: Says a secure border is essential to prevent criminals and narcotics from crossing into El Paso, and supports the Customs and Border Protection mission.
